title: The Crooked Salt
premise: Emrys Fairweather, the last swordspeaker bound by an oath of silence, keeps the ledgers of the Crooked Salt, a guild that trades in impossible things—bottled storms, borrowed years, names not yet earned. When a child named Sable arrives speaking a language older than kingdoms, Emrys recognizes it as the tongue that once commanded blades to sing and started the Sundering War. As the guild's rivals and the Crown's inquisitors close in during the falling long winter, Emrys must choose between the oath that defines them and the found family forming around Sable. In the end, Emrys breaks their vow—not to fight, but to speak the child's language aloud, unbinding the old magic into something new and ending the war before it begins.
about_author: Wendell Zhou is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing trade ledgers from defunct merchant guilds before turning to fiction. They write quiet fantasies about people whose jobs are stranger than their adventures.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. A quiet night at the Crooked Salt guildhouse: Emrys catalogs a bottled storm and a vial of borrowed courage, establishing the guild's rules and their own oath-bound silence—swordspeakers may never speak the old tongue. The beat is loneliness disguised as contentment; Emrys insists invisibility is safety.

chapters.title: A Knock in the Snow
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. During the first hard snowfall, a starving child arrives at the door with no name but one word: Sable. When she speaks, Emrys hears the pre-kingdom tongue—the language of the Sundering—and nearly turns her away. The emotional beat is terror warring with pity; Emrys lets her in and immediately regrets it.

chapters.title: What the Guild Owes
chapters.summary: POV Maren, the guild's quartermaster and Emrys's reluctant friend. She argues the Crooked Salt has always sheltered impossible things, so Sable qualifies. Emrys tests Sable's language against sealed guild records and finds matches. Beat: grudging alliance; Maren forces Emrys to admit they care already.

chapters.title: The Inquisitor's Coin
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. A Crown inquisitor arrives as a customer, paying in suspiciously fresh coin, asking about 'a child who speaks wrong.' Emrys lies for the first time in twenty years of oaths. Beat: dread and exhilaration—the lie feels like breaking ice. Emrys realizes someone informed on them.

chapters.title: Songs the Blades Remember
chapters.summary: POV Sable. Through her eyes we learn fragments: she was sent to find 'the one who keeps words,' fleeing soldiers who burned her village. Her language isn't just speech—it makes objects remember what they were. A rusted sword hums when she sings. Beat: wonder shadowed by grief and survivor's guilt.

chapters.title: The Traitor's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Maren. Auditing the books, Maren finds entries in a hand she knows—a senior guild member has been selling information to the Crown. Confronted, he argues the guild's survival requires sacrifice. Beat: betrayal inside the found family; Maren must choose loyalty to the guild or its people.

chapters.title: Oath and Ember
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. The inquisitor returns with soldiers; the traitor opens the door. In the chaos, Sable is taken, and Emrys's suppressed magic erupts—every blade in the room remembers being sung to. Emrys escapes with wounds and shame. Beat: rock bottom; the cost of silence made flesh.

chapters.title: The Long Winter's Price
chapters.summary: POV Emrys and Maren alternating. The guild fractures—some flee, some stay. Emrys confesses everything: the oath, the war, why swordspeakers were silenced. Maren offers not forgiveness but partnership. Beat: vulnerability met with acceptance; the found family chooses each other deliberately.

chapters.title: Where the Words Were Kept
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Emrys infiltrates the inquisitor's fortress-prison where Sable is held, discovering the Crown wants her as a weapon to reignite the Sundering. Emrys reaches her cell and, instead of fighting, does the unthinkable: answers her in the old tongue. Beat: climax of love against duty; the oath shatters.

chapters.title: The New Tongue
chapters.summary: POV Sable, closing with Emrys. Together they speak a hybrid language—old words given new meaning—and the magic unbinds rather than ignites: weapons across the fortress forget how to hate. The war dies unborn; the traitor and inquisitor face consequences; the Crooked Salt reopens its doors. Beat: resolution—Sable gains a family, Emrys gains a voice.
